results.title: Derived subgroups under a commutator power identity (Kourovka 13.34)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the proposition that for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every group $G$ with $[x, y]^n = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$, every element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ has finite order, that is, the derived subgroup of $G$ is periodic.

results.title: A commutator power identity need not make the derived subgroup periodic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist an integer $n \ge 1$ and a group $G$ such that $[x, y]^n = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$ but some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ has infinite order. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 13.34 (I. D. Macdonald; V. D. Mazurov) in the negative, by results of G. S. Deryabina and P. A. Kozhevnikov from 1999 and of S. I. Adyan from 2000.

results.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is the real number $\mu((x, \infty))$ when $\mu((x, \infty)) < \infty$, and $0$ when $\mu((x, \infty)) = \infty$.

results.title: Left tail of a measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a real $x$, the left tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is the real number $\mu((-\infty, -x))$, where an infinite value is sent to $0$.

results.title: Combined tail of a measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a real number $x$, the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is the real number $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$, where each of the two measures is converted from $[0, \infty]$ to a real number, an infinite value becoming $0$.

results.title: The right tail of a probability measure is at most one

results.title: The left tail of a probability measure is at most one

results.title: The combined tail of a probability measure is at most two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every real number $x$, the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$ satisfies $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x)) \le 2$.

results.title: The right tail of a finite measure is antitone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$. If $x \le y$, then the right tail of $\mu$ at $y$ is at most the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the left tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the left tail of $\mu$ is antitone in the threshold: if $a \le b$, then $\mu((-\infty, -b)) \le \mu((-\infty, -a))$.

results.title: The combined tail is antitone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and write $T(x) = \mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$ for its combined tail at a real number $x$. Then $T$ is antitone: $T(b) \le T(a)$ whenever $a \le b$.

results.title: The right tail is at most the combined tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the right tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is at most the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$.

results.title: The left tail is at most the combined tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every real $x$, the left tail of $\mu$ at $x$ is at most the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$.

results.title: The right tail of a finite measure vanishes at infinity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the right tail $\mu((x, \infty))$, taken as a real number, tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: The left tail of a finite measure vanishes at infinity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the left tail $\mu((-\infty, -x))$, taken as a real number, tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: The combined tail of a finite measure vanishes at infinity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the combined tail $\mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$, with both masses taken as real numbers, tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: Tail balance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and $p$ a real number. Write $R(x) = \mu((x, \infty))$ for the right tail and $T(x) = \mu((x, \infty)) + \mu((-\infty, -x))$ for the combined tail of $\mu$. The measure $\mu$ has tail balance $p$ when $0 \le p \le 1$, $T(x) > 0$ for all sufficiently large $x$, and $R(x) / T(x) \to p$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: Tail balance zero from a vanishing right tail

results.title: Eventually vanishing combined tail rules out tail balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and let $p \in \mathbb{R}$. If the combined tail of $\mu$ at $x$ equals $0$ for all sufficiently large $x$, then $\mu$ does not have tail balance $p$.

results.title: Dirac masses have no tail balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and every $p \in \mathbb{R}$, the Dirac measure $\delta_a$ at $a$ does not have tail balance $p$.

results.title: Karamata's integral theorem

results.title: Sharpness of the Ising phase transition on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Sharpness of the phase transition for the Ising model on `ℤ^d`, `d ≥ 2`: for `β ≥ β_c`, `m*(β) ≥ √(1 - (β_c/β)²)`; for `0 ≤ β < β_c`, the plus-state two-point function `z ↦ ⟨σ_0σ_z⟩^+_β` is summable and decays as `exp(-c‖z‖₁)`. Reference: H. Duminil-Copin, V. Tassion, "A new proof of the sharpness of the phase transition for Bernoulli percolation and the Ising model", Comm. Math. Phys. 343 (2016) 725–745, Theorem…
